official_sources.title: Central Committee / State Council, Outline Development Plan for the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, Chapter 3, Section 1
official_sources.finding: The official plan names Hong Kong–Shenzhen, Guangzhou–Foshan, and Macao–Zhuhai as cooperation poles. This supports those three Atlas parent labels as policy/geographic groupings; it does not make them official provinces or administrative parents.
official_sources.reuse: No blanket reuse license was located. The locally retained response is attributed for internal evidence and is not presented as freely redistributable.

official_sources.title: Hong Kong Basic Law, Chapter I, Articles 1–2
official_sources.finding: The Basic Law states Hong Kong is an inalienable part of the PRC and has a separate SAR constitutional and administrative framework. Preserve atlas:territory:HKG as a distinct source identity; do not treat the Shenzhen cooperation-pole parent as a legal parent.
official_sources.reuse: Official legal text; no page-specific redistribution terms reviewed.

official_sources.title: Hong Kong Basic Law, Preamble
official_sources.finding: The preamble establishes the SAR legal context. It is not a polygon source.

official_sources.title: Macao SAR Government Portal, Constitutional Documents
official_sources.finding: Macao is established as a Special Administrative Region under PRC Constitution Article 31 and its Basic Law. Preserve atlas:territory:MAC separately; the Macao–Zhuhai parent is a policy pole, not a legal administrative parent.

official_sources.title: Hainan Statistical Yearbook 2024, table 1-1: Divisions of Administrative Areas (2023)
official_sources.access: Official web search index exposed the table text; direct page/PDF retrieval returned HTTP 403 in this environment, so original PDF bytes/hash are not claimed.
official_sources.restoration: Re-fetch the exact official PDF URL, retain the original bytes, record response date, length and SHA-256, then inspect printed page 3/table 1-1.
official_sources.finding: The 2023 official table lists 19 administrative place rows, including Wuzhishan, Wenchang, Sansha, Danzhou, Haikou, and Sanya. The issue's Hainan scope has 18 rows and no Wuzhishan; it includes separate Qiongshan City and Haikou rows. The 2017 source name Qiongshan City therefore needs modern district crosswalk review.

official_sources.access: Official search-indexed primary source; direct page retrieval returned HTTP 403 in this environment; no original byte hash is claimed.

This corroborates the Wenchang/Sansha parent conflict and Wuzhishan omission.

research_limits: Official current county-level legal boundary bytes and reuse conditions have not been recovered for the 198 mainland China source features.

The current 2025 Hainan yearbook official listing is known, but its exact table bytes were unavailable; the 2024 yearbook's 2023 table and official 2024 bulletin support the identified roster discrepancy.

No current legal polygon overlay, boundary validity, gap/overlap, coastline/island completeness, or neighbor-alignment test was performed for Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Hong Kong, Macao, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, Yunnan, Vietnam, or South China Sea island units.
The Natural Earth HKG/MAC member IDs are reproducible from retained Admin 1 DBF rows; this does not certify source geometry against current official SAR boundaries.

The 2017 source has no official locality code or parent key. Present-day parent support for every mainland row therefore remains incomplete even when current framework labels and source names appear plausible.
